Log of the claims checked in a session

Source: R/csdg_claim_log.R
csdg_claim_log.Rd

The package keeps an append-only log of the claims of the current R session: every claim derived with claim_relies_mainly(), claim_top_k(), claim_order(), or claim_direction(), and every call of csdg_check(), csdg_assess(), and csdg_confirm(). csdg_claim_log() returns the log, and csdg_claim_log_reset() empties it, for example at the start of an analysis.

The article asks researchers to report every claim they checked, including the claims that were not met or remained unresolved, because a claim selected from many tried claims is more likely to be met by chance and readers can judge this only if they know what was tried. The log records this list as the analysis runs, so that it does not depend on memory; csdg_export_assessment() writes it alongside an assessment (claim_log.csv). The log holds no row-level data: the data are identified by the task id, their dimensions, and a hash. It is kept in memory only and is lost when the R session ends or the package is reloaded.

Usage

csdg_claim_log()

csdg_claim_log_reset()

Value

csdg_claim_log(): a data.table::data.table() with one row per entry and the columns entry (running number), time (UTC), function_name, claim_id, kind ("relies_mainly", "top_k", "order", or "direction"), statement (the wording of the claim), quantity ("pfi", "loco", or "ale"), learners (labels of the learners the claim covers), task_id, n_rows, n_features, data_hash (SHA-256 hash of the task data, the hash that csdg_fit() stores), origin ("exploratory" or "tested on new data"), and result (empty for derived claims; the worst status per required gate for csdg_check(); the label of the assessment for csdg_assess() and csdg_confirm()). csdg_claim_log_reset(): the log before it was emptied, invisibly.

See also

csdg_export_assessment()

Examples

csdg_claim_log_reset()
set.seed(1)
n = 200
x = data.frame(a = rnorm(n), b = rnorm(n), c = rnorm(n))
x$y = 2 * x$a + x$b + rnorm(n)
task = mlr3::as_task_regr(x, target = "y", id = "toy")
imp = csdg_importance(csdg_fit(task, list(tree = mlr3::lrn("regr.rpart")), folds = 3, seed = 1),
  repetitions = 5, seed = 2)
claim = claim_order(imp, "a", "b")
res = csdg_assess(csdg_check(claim, imp))
csdg_claim_log()[, .(entry, function_name, statement, result)]
#>    entry function_name                                 statement
#>    <int>        <char>                                    <char>
#> 1:     1   claim_order Decision tree relies more on a than on b.
#> 2:     2    csdg_check Decision tree relies more on a than on b.
#> 3:     3   csdg_assess Decision tree relies more on a than on b.
#>                               result
#>                               <char>
#> 1:                              <NA>
#> 2: open: G0b; supported: G0a, G2, G5
#> 3:          unresolved (exploratory)
